hints: Notice the speed is $12 \text{ m}$ per minute, so first convert it to $\text{m s}^{-1}$ by dividing by $60$.
For lifting at constant speed, the upward force equals the weight $mg$ and useful power is $P = Fv$.
Multiply $600 \text{ kg} \times 9.81 \text{ N kg}^{-1} \times 0.20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and then convert watts to kilowatts.
walkthrough: Convert the rising speed to SI units: $v = 12/60 = 0.20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ because power needs $\text{m s}^{-1}$, not per minute.
At constant vertical speed the resultant force is zero, so the motor pulls up with force equal to the weight: $F = mg = 600 \times 9.81 \text{ N}$.
Calculate $P \approx 5886 \times 0.20 \approx 1180 \text{ W} \approx 1.2 \text{ kW}$. This is option B.

options.A: Gives $120 \text{ W}$, ten times too small, from an error with $g$ or with the minute to second conversion.
options.B: Equals $mgv$ with $v$ in $\text{m s}^{-1}$, about $600 \times 9.81 \times 0.20 \approx 1200 \text{ W}$.
options.C: Uses $mv$ instead of $mgv$, giving $600 \times 12 = 7200 \text{ W}$ and omitting weight.
options.D: Uses $12 \text{ m}$ per minute as $12 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, giving about $600 \times 9.81 \times 12 \approx 71 \text{ kW}$.
